document_scope.title: ACKS Core - Equipment, Encumbrance, Hirelings, Henchmen, Mercenaries, and Specialists
document_scope.focus: Mechanical rules, procedures, definitions, and tables only.

starting_equipment.default_clothing: All characters begin with sturdy clothes suitable for adventuring.
starting_equipment.starting_wealth: Additional starting equipment is purchased with 3d6 x 10 gp.

class_relevance.note: Characters are expected to buy equipment appropriate to class needs.

row.common_professions: skilled laborers or journeyman crafters; 1st level adventurers
master craftsmen or yeomen farmer (85 acres); 2nd level adventurers
master professionals or landed patrician (200 acres); 3rd-4th level adventurers
barons or wealthy patricians; 5th-7th level adventurers

purchasing_equipment.recordkeeping: All purchases should be recorded on the character sheet, including remaining money.
purchasing_equipment.open_item_creation: If desired items are not listed, the Judge may derive characteristics and prices from existing items.

class_restriction_rule.statement: Any class may purchase, carry, and use any weapon or armor.

penalty_when_using_prohibited_equipment.effect: Character fights as a 0-level character while so equipped.
No bonus on attack throws or armor class from ability scores or equipment.

market.description: major ports, national capitals, other large cities

equipment_availability_rules.rule: Availability is determined by item price category relative to market class.
Values are the number of each specific item available each month, not total items in that price category.
Percentages indicate the chance that one unit of that specific item is available at all that month.
equipment_availability_rules.bundle_rule: Bundles of small items sold together count as one item for availability purposes.

commissioning_equipment.availability_adjustment: Commissioned equipment is treated as one price category less expensive when determining whether builders/trainers are available.
commissioning_equipment.drawback: Commissioned goods are not immediately available.

time_to_complete.category: 1 day per 1gp value to find and train

weapons.damage_note: Where two damage values are listed, the first is for one-handed use and the second is for two-handed use.

item.name: Great Axe
item.effect: Imposes -1 penalty on initiative rolls.

item.name: Belladonna
item.effect: If eaten within 1 hour of infection with lycanthropy, character may save vs Poison to shake off lycanthropy.
item.failure: If the save fails, the character dies from poison after 1 turn.
item.limitation: Even if poison is neutralized or the character is raised, the lycanthropy remains; further doses are useless.

item.name: Birthwort
item.requirement: Must be applied by an adventurer with the Healing proficiency.
item.effect: Provides +2 bonus on Healing proficiency throw to neutralize poison.

item.name: Bola
item.effect: May be used with a thrown attack to make a knock down or wrestling maneuver.

item.name: Longbow
item.restriction: Cannot be used by mounted troops.

item.name: Candles
item.effect: Dimly illuminate a 5' radius.
item.special: Tallow candles produce foul-smelling smoke; adventurers carrying them never surprise creatures with keen olfactory senses.

item.name: Canoe
item.overland_transport: Can be carried overland by two people at a cost of 5 stone of encumbrance.

item.name: Cart, Small
item.mobility: May only move through desert, mountains, forests, or swamps if a road is available.

item.name: Cart, Large
item.mobility: May only move through desert, mountains, forests, or swamps if a road is available.

option.team: 1 heavy horse or 2 mules or 2 medium horses

item.name: Military Oil
item.effect: May be thrown at a creature, dealing 1d8 damage for 2 rounds to the creature struck.
May be poured on the floor and ignited to delay pursuit.
item.special: Cannot be easily doused with water.

level.effect: +1 to Performance proficiency throws made with it
+2 to Performance proficiency throws made with it

item.name: Net
item.effect: Provides +2 bonus on attack throws to wrestle opponents.

item.name: Pole, Wooden
item.use: Commonly used to prod or test hazardous areas and measure depth.

item.name: Pole Arm
item.effect: Can attack from the second rank in melee.
Inflicts double damage when used in or against a charge.

item.name: Raft/Barge
item.barge: Professionally built barges can be 30' x 40' and carry 500 stone (5,000lb) per 10' square.
item.makeshift_raft: Makeshift rafts can be up to 20' x 30'; each 10' square carries 250 stone (2,500lb).
item.construction_time: Makeshift raft construction takes 1d3 days per 10' x 10' portion.

item.name: Rations, Iron
item.duration: Last 2 months in wilderness, 1 week in dungeon conditions.

item.name: Rations, Standard
item.duration: Last 1 week in wilderness; spoil overnight in dank dungeons.

item.name: Saddle and Tack

types.type: Used to harness to cart or wagon or carry saddle bags; cannot be used for riding.

item.combat_rule: Without a military saddle, a rider in combat must save vs Paralysis each time he is dealt damage or be knocked off the horse.

item.name: Sailing Ship, Large
item.weapon_mounts: May mount up to 2 light catapults.

item.name: Sap
item.effect: Provides +2 bonus to attack throws made to incapacitate opponents.

item.name: Shield
item.effect: Increases AC by 1 while equipped.
item.limitations: No protection when surprised, retreating, or attacked from behind.

item.name: Spear
item.effect: Can be used one- or two-handed.
Can attack from the second rank in melee.
Inflicts double damage when used in or against a charge.

item.name: Spell Book (Blank)
item.recording_rule: Each spell uses one page per spell level.

item.name: Staff
item.effect: Used two-handed; if used one-handed, treat as a club.

item.name: Two-Handed Sword
item.effect: Imposes -1 penalty on initiative rolls.

item.name: Thieves' Tools
item.requirement: Required to make proficiency throws to open locks and remove traps.

item.name: Tinderbox
item.timing: Lighting a torch takes a full round.
Lighting any other fire with flint and steel takes at least a full round.

item.name: Torch
item.combat_damage: Deals 1d4 damage if used in combat.

item.name: Troop Transport, Large
item.capacity: Can carry 50 marines in addition to its normal complement of 20 sailors.

item.name: Troop Transport, Small
item.capacity: Can carry 25 marines in addition to its normal complement of 12 sailors.

item.name: Wagon
item.mobility: Moves under the same speed and terrain conditions as a cart.

item.name: Whip
item.effect: Provides +2 bonus to attack throws made to disarm or knock down opponents.

item.name: Wolfsbane
item.effect: If a character strikes a lycanthrope in melee with a sprig of wolfsbane and the target fails a save vs Poison, it must flee as if turned.
item.risk: A character who eats wolfsbane must save vs Poison or die after 1 turn.

item.name: Woundwart
item.requirement: Must be used by an adventurer with Healing proficiency.
item.effect: Provides +2 bonus on proficiency throws to cure light wounds and cure serious wounds.

definitions.encumbrance: Measure of how much equipment and treasure a character carries.
definitions.stone: A unit treated as about 10lb, abstracted to represent weight, bulk, and portability.

row.encumbrance: 1 stone per point of Armor Class

encumbrance_rules.magic_armor_rule: Magical armor and shields reduce encumbrance by 1 stone per point of magical bonus.
encumbrance_rules.item_counting_rule: Each weapon, scroll, potion, vial, wand, magic item, or similar object counts as one item.
encumbrance_rules.bundle_rule: Bundles of small items count as one item.
encumbrance_rules.tiny_item_rule: Very small single items such as one silver arrow can be ignored for encumbrance.

heavy_item_definition.criterion: Two-handed weapons, including bows and crossbows.
Items as tall as the carrier, including spears, staffs, and 10' poles.
Items requiring two hands to carry, such as chairs or chests.

encumbrance_rules.heavier_than_stone_rule: Items over 14lb weigh more than 1 stone.
encumbrance_rules.container_conversion_rule: Container capacity listed in stone converts to coins at 1 stone : 1,000 coins.

animal_vehicle_movement_rule.definition: The value to the left of the slash is movement per turn when carrying normal load or less; the value to the right is movement per turn when carrying more than normal load but not more than maximum load.

types.type: NPC sidekicks/companions. Generally loyal. Usually the only hirelings willing to accompany adventurers into dungeons, lairs, or ruins.
Hired soldiers for guard, patrol, or war service in wilderness or military forces; not normal adventuring companions.
Hired experts with a trade or special knowledge, usually for specific tasks.

availability_rules.rule: Hirelings are limited by market class.
Percentages indicate chance that at least one of that hireling type is present.

timing.week_1: One-half of available hirelings, rounded up.

search_costs.rule: Each week spent searching for hirelings costs the listed fee per hireling type.

general_hiring_terms.henchmen: Typically hired for a share of treasure of at least 15% of the employer's income, plus monthly fee for food, lodging, and expenses based on level.
general_hiring_terms.mercenaries: Typically hired for a flat monthly fee.
general_hiring_terms.specialists: Typically hired for a flat monthly fee.
general_hiring_terms.equipment: Henchmen, mercenaries, and specialists normally have equipment appropriate to profession/class/level; adventurers may provide extra equipment.

procedure.step: Modify by employer's Charisma bonus or penalty.
Judge may apply situational modifiers, usually around +/-1 for better or worse terms; similar modest adjustments are allowed.

results.refuse_and_slander: Future reaction rolls in that town or region suffer -1 toward that adventurer.
results.try_again: NPC needs a sweeter deal; if no improved offer is made, treat as Refuse.
results.accept: NPC becomes the character's hireling on stated terms.
results.accept_with_elan: As Accept, plus the hireling gets +1 on morale rolls.

special_notes.note: Mounted crossbowmen are only found in Dwarven settlements.
Beast Riders are only found in Chaotic-aligned settlements.

henchmen.generation: Henchmen are rolled up like player characters, with ability scores, class, hit points, and equipment.

eligibility_by_employer_level.rule: Potential henchmen should be lower level than their employer.
A 1st level character can hire only normal men.
A 2nd level character can hire only 1st level characters.
eligibility_by_employer_level.trigger: If a henchman concludes he is more powerful than his employer, make an immediate Henchman Loyalty roll.
eligibility_by_employer_level.market_limit: Henchmen above 4th level are not generally for hire on the market, though they may be found on adventures.

morale.base: Generally 0 plus employer's Charisma bonus or penalty.
morale.judge_adjustment: May be increased for especially good treatment or reduced for cruelty or broken word.

when_to_roll.event: Whenever a henchman suffers a calamity.
At the end of each adventure if the henchman leveled up.

morale.roll_method: Roll 2d6 and add henchman's morale; Judge may usually adjust by no more than +/-2 for pay and treatment.

loyalty_results.hostility: Henchman leaves and becomes a rival/enemy; can never again be recruited by that character.
loyalty_results.resignation: Henchman leaves without ill will and may be recruited again later.
loyalty_results.grudging_loyalty: Henchman stays reluctantly; if terms are not improved, the next loyalty roll is at -1.
loyalty_results.fanatic_loyalty: Henchman becomes dedicated and sworn servant; all future morale rolls are at +2.

morale_score_changes.penalty: Morale permanently decreases by 1 each time the henchman suffers a calamity.
morale_score_changes.bonus: Morale permanently increases by 1 each time the henchman gains a level while in the adventurer's service.

maximum_henchmen.rule: A player character may have at most 4 henchmen, modified by Charisma bonus or penalty.
maximum_henchmen.overflow_attempt: Trying to hire more than this causes the character to lose one existing henchman.
maximum_henchmen.exemption: Mercenaries and specialists do not count against this limit.

experience.rule: Henchmen who participate in an adventure gain XP.
experience.share: Each henchman receives one-half of a normal XP share.

mercenaries.service_limits: Mercenaries usually garrison strongholds or fight in military campaigns; they do not accompany employers on dangerous adventures such as dungeon exploration unless they become henchmen.

costing.not_included: Armorers, stablehands, caravans, supplies in the field, and other incidental expenses.
costing.campaign_expectation: Mercenaries on campaign expect a share of military plunder in addition to wages.

morale.base: Based on training and equipment, not employer Charisma.
morale.situational_modifiers: Working conditions may raise or lower morale.

examples.low: If being killed frequently or abused.

Light Infantry (3 javelins, short sword, shield, leather armor)
Heavy Infantry (spear, sword, shield, banded plate armor)
Slingers (sling, short sword, shield, leather armor)

Mounted Crossbowmen (crossbow, short sword, chainmail, mule)
Horse Archers (composite bow, scimitar, leather armor, light warhorse)

specialists.general_rule: The list is not exhaustive; the Judge may create more specialists using proficiency rules.
specialists.player_character_option: Player characters with appropriate proficiencies may serve as specialists.

effects.effect: May assist mages in potion creation.
May research new potions as if a 5th level mage.
effects.limitation: Research takes twice the base time and cost.

specialist.name: Animal Trainer
specialist.scope: The least expensive trainer handles one type of normal animal; trainers able to handle multiple types or monsters cost more.

training_time.taming_minimum: At least 1 month to tame a wild animal.
training_time.behavior_minimum: At least 1 month to teach one behavior to an already tame animal.
training_time.additional_behaviors: After the first month, additional behaviors for that same animal take half time per behavior.

interruptions.behavior_training_interrupted: All time spent on that behavior is lost.
interruptions.taming_interrupted: The animal rebels and can never be tamed.

specialist.capacity: One trainer can train and manage no more than 6 animals at a time.
specialist.after_training: Once fully trained and in service, the trainer is no longer needed to handle it.

specialist.name: Armorer
specialist.production: Produces 40gp worth of weapons, armor, or shields per month.
specialist.maintenance_requirement: Required at a rate of 1 armorer per 60 troops to maintain and repair armor and weapons.

specialist.name: Engineer
specialist.function: Plans and oversees large construction projects such as strongholds.

specialist.name: Healer
specialist.common_effect: Under treatment in clean sanitary conditions with bed rest, a patient regains an extra 1d3 hit points per day.

physicker.effect: May non-magically neutralize poison, cure disease, or cure light wounds with a proficiency throw of 18+ once per day per patient.

chirugeon.effect: May non-magically neutralize poison, cure disease, or cure serious wounds with a proficiency throw of 14+ once per day per patient.

type.name: navigator
type.role: required when a ship ventures beyond sight of coast

specialist.name: Ruffian
specialist.uses: May be used as muscle or sent on hijinks such as assassinating, carousing, spying, stealing, or treasure-hunting.
specialist.responsibility: If caught during hijinks, they expect the employer to rescue or bail them out.
specialist.adventure_limit: Do not go on adventures unless recruited as henchmen.
specialist.advancement: May gain XP from hijinks; if they level up, use the Henchmen Monthly Fee table for higher wages.

specialist.name: Sage
specialist.availability: Sages are rare and usually specialize in a subject area.
specialist.additional_costs: Difficult questions may require extra research costs and supplies beyond monthly pay.
specialist.uncertainty: The Judge decides what is obscure and the chance a wrong answer is given; characters may not realize an answer is wrong.

specialist.name: Spellcaster
specialist.use: Arcane or divine casters may be hired to cast spells for adventurers.
specialist.availability: Determined by market class and spell level.
specialist.casting_limit: Each available spellcaster can cast a spell of the listed level once per day.
specialist.recruitment_rule: Availability does not guarantee cooperation; the caster must still be successfully hired through negotiation.

cleric_restrictions.restriction: Clerics never cast spells for adventurers of opposite alignment.
cleric_restrictions.surcharge: Clerics may charge double if adventurers do not belong to their faith.
